## Xi Jinping in 2024: `1B.8` crisis de-escalation and accident-risk communication

Best read: **I found some evidence of clear public reassurance and de-escalatory messaging, but no strong evidence of actual crisis-management behavior or preserved wartime communication channels.** The negative side is mostly indirect: coercive Taiwan drills, nuclear buildup, and Rocket Force instability all raise accidental-war risk.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Supports `1B.8` | [China's nuclear policy remains stable, consistent and predictable: spokesperson](https://eng.mod.gov.cn/xb/News_213114/NewsRelease/16341310.html) | PRC Ministry of National Defense | 2024-09-26 | https://eng.mod.gov.cn/xb/News_213114/NewsRelease/16341310.html | After China’s September ICBM launch, the spokesperson said the nuclear policy is stable, consistent, predictable, and based on no-first-use and minimum required capability. This is the clearest 2024 post-event reassurance and fits clearer communication in a tense moment. | `1B.8`, `1B.2`, `1B.3` |
| Supports `1B.8` | [No-first-use of Nuclear Weapons Initiative](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202407/t20240723_11458632.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-07-23 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202407/t20240723_11458632.html | Official paper says Xi re-affirmed that nuclear weapons cannot be used and nuclear war must not be fought, and reiterates no-first-use. That is crisis-reducing messaging, though it is declaratory rather than operational. | `1B.8`, `1B.1`, `1B.2`, `1B.4` |
| Supports `1B.8` | [China's nuclear arms control position paper](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/gjhdq_665435/3376_665447/3432_664920/3435_664926/202406/t20240612_11428155.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-06-12 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/gjhdq_665435/3376_665447/3432_664920/3435_664926/202406/t20240612_11428155.html | China urged nuclear-weapon states to reduce the role of nuclear weapons, avoid launch-on-warning or pre-emptive doctrines, and avoid actions that spur arms races. This is explicit de-escalatory language aimed at lowering accidental-war risk. | `1B.8`, `1B.4`, `1B.1` |
| Supports `1B.8` | [Wang Yi elaborates on China's position on Ukraine crisis](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/zyxw/202405/t20240530_11332760.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-02-18 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/zyxw/202405/t20240530_11332760.html | Wang Yi attributed to Xi the position that nuclear weapons must not be used and nuclear wars must not be fought, and said China should protect nuclear materials and facilities while pursuing a peaceful settlement of the Ukraine crisis. This supports crisis de-escalation language. | `1B.8`, `1B.1`, `1B.2` |
| Cuts against `1B.8` | [PLA conducts joint military drills surrounding Taiwan Island](https://eng.mod.gov.cn/xb/News_213114/TopStories/16310652.html) | PRC Ministry of National Defense / Xinhua | 2024-05-23 | https://eng.mod.gov.cn/xb/News_213114/TopStories/16310652.html | The PLA announced combat-readiness patrols, precision strikes, and a “stern warning” to Taiwan independence forces. This is coercive signaling in a flashpoint, not crisis de-escalation, and it increases accidental-war risk. | `1B.8`, `6A` |
| Cuts against `1B.8` | [Reuters report on Rocket Force purges](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3270993/chinas-communist-party-targets-another-pla-general-corruption-investigation?UUID=f0bc4b91-7818-4f96-bf67-aa5b46ac9395&next_article_id=3270939&tc=7&tpcc=enlz-globalimpact) | South China Morning Post / Reuters | 2024-07-18 | https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3270993/chinas-communist-party-targets-another-pla-general-corruption-investigation?UUID=f0bc4b91-7818-4f96-bf67-aa5b46ac9395&next_article_id=3270939&tc=7&tpcc=enlz-globalimpact | Reuters reported another Rocket Force senior officer was expelled amid a broader purge of officers overseeing China’s nuclear arsenal. That suggests instability inside the force responsible for strategic missiles, which is bad for accident prevention and crisis reliability. | `1B.8`, `1B.3`, `7B` |
| Cuts against `1B.8` | [Role of nuclear weapons grows as geopolitical relations deteriorate - new SIPRI Yearbook out now](https://www.sipri.org/media/press-release/2024/role-nuclear-weapons-grows-geopolitical-relations-deteriorate-new-sipri-yearbook-out-now) | SIPRI | 2024-06-17 | https://www.sipri.org/media/press-release/2024/role-nuclear-weapons-grows-geopolitical-relations-deteriorate-new-sipri-yearbook-out-now | SIPRI said China’s arsenal rose from 410 to 500 warheads and warned some warheads may be on missiles in peacetime. That is not crisis communication, but it is counterevidence to a low-risk posture. | `1B.8`, `1B.1` |

### Synthesis

- **Best support:** China’s public messaging in 2024 was usually calm, predictable, and explicitly anti-nuclear-use.
- **Best counterevidence:** China still used coercive military signaling around Taiwan, expanded nuclear forces, and had discipline problems inside the Rocket Force.
- **Overall judgment for `1B.8`:** **some support on messaging, weak evidence on actual crisis-management practice.** I found no solid 2024 source showing Xi personally preserved hotlines, opened de-escalation channels, or managed a live nuclear crisis in a way that clearly reduced accidental-war risk.

### Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence of:
- a live crisis in which Xi clearly de-escalated,
- a new or renewed hotline / communication channel,
- a public confidence-building measure with Taiwan, the US, or another nuclear-armed state,
- or an operational accident-prevention mechanism beyond declaratory policy.

So the record is **rhetorically de-escalatory, operationally unproven**.
